title: Every product
task: Show every column of every row in the products table.
answer: SELECT * FROM products;

title: Names and prices
task: Show just product_name and list_price for every product.
answer: SELECT product_name, list_price FROM products;

title: First ten orders
task: Show the first 10 rows of orders, in order of order_id.
answer: SELECT * FROM orders ORDER BY order_id LIMIT 10;

title: Profit per product
task: For each product, show product_name and the profit per unit (list_price - unit_cost) as a column called margin.
answer: SELECT product_name, list_price - unit_cost AS margin FROM products;

title: Lighting products
task: Show the name and price of every product in the Lighting category.
answer: SELECT product_name, list_price FROM products WHERE category = 'Lighting';

title: Most expensive first
task: List products that cost more than $150, most expensive first. Show name and price.
answer: SELECT product_name, list_price FROM products WHERE list_price > 150 ORDER BY list_price DESC;

title: Find the candles
task: Show every product whose name contains the word Candle.
answer: SELECT * FROM products WHERE product_name LIKE '%Candle%';

title: Missing cities
task: Show the customers who have no city recorded.
answer: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE city IS NULL;

title: Black Friday weekend
task: Show orders placed from 28 November to 1 December 2025 (inclusive) that used a discount code.
answer: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE order_date BETWEEN '2025-11-28' AND '2025-12-01' AND discount_code IS NOT NULL;

title: How many orders?
task: How many orders were delivered? Return one number.
answer: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM orders WHERE status = 'delivered';

title: Products per category
task: Show each category and how many products it has, biggest first.
answer: SELECT category, COUNT(*) AS products FROM products GROUP BY category ORDER BY products DESC, category;

title: Discount codes
task: For each discount code, show how many orders used it and the total discount given. Leave out orders with no code.
answer: SELECT discount_code, COUNT(*) AS orders, ROUND(SUM(discount), 2) AS total_discount FROM orders WHERE discount_code IS NOT NULL GROUP BY discount_code;

title: Common return reasons
task: Show return reasons that happened more than 70 times, with their counts.
answer: SELECT reason, COUNT(*) AS returns FROM returns GROUP BY reason HAVING COUNT(*) > 70;

title: Price bands
task: Put products into bands — Under $50, $50–$149, $150 and over — and count the products in each band.
answer: SELECT CASE WHEN list_price < 50 THEN 'Under $50' WHEN list_price < 150 THEN '$50–$149' ELSE '$150 and over' END AS band, COUNT(*) FROM products GROUP BY band;

title: Who ordered?
task: Show each order's order_id, order_date and the customer's first and last name.
answer: SELECT o.order_id, o.order_date, c.first_name, c.last_name FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id;

title: Revenue by category
task: Show each product category and its revenue (quantity × unit_price) from delivered orders, highest first, rounded to cents.
answer: SELECT p.category, ROUND(SUM(i.quantity * i.unit_price), 2) AS revenue FROM order_items i JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = i.order_id JOIN products p ON p.product_id = i.product_id WHERE o.status = 'delivered' GROUP BY p.category ORDER BY revenue DESC;

title: Customers who never ordered
task: Show customers who have never placed an order.
answer: SELECT c.* FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE o.order_id IS NULL;

title: Customers by channel
task: Show each marketing channel's name and how many customers signed up through it.
answer: SELECT ch.channel_name, COUNT(c.customer_id) FROM channels ch LEFT JOIN customers c ON c.channel_id = ch.channel_id GROUP BY ch.channel_name;

title: Monthly orders
task: Show each month of 2025 (as YYYY-MM) and how many delivered orders it had, in date order.
answer: SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', order_date) AS month, COUNT(*) FROM orders WHERE status = 'delivered' GROUP BY month ORDER BY month;

title: Above-average products
task: Show products whose list_price is above the average list price.
answer: SELECT * FROM products WHERE list_price > (SELECT AVG(list_price) FROM products);

title: Rank within category
task: For every product, show its category, name, price and its price rank within its category (1 = most expensive), using RANK().
answer: SELECT category, product_name, list_price, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY category ORDER BY list_price DESC) AS price_rank FROM products;

title: Running total
task: Using a CTE of monthly revenue (delivered orders), show each month, its revenue and a running total for the year, in date order. Round both to cents.
answer: WITH monthly AS (SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', o.order_date) AS month, SUM(i.quantity * i.unit_price) AS revenue FROM orders o JOIN order_items i ON i.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'delivered' GROUP BY month) SELECT month, ROUND(revenue, 2), ROUND(SUM(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY month), 2) FROM monthly ORDER BY month;

module: 6. Clean data and tell the story
title: Messy states
task: Show each different way state was typed in customers, and how many customers used it.
answer: SELECT state, COUNT(*) FROM customers GROUP BY state;

module: 6. Clean data and tell the story
title: Clean the states
task: Count customers per state after cleaning: make Vic, Victoria → VIC, nsw, New South Wales → NSW, Qld → QLD, W.A. → WA and Tas → TAS.
answer: SELECT CASE WHEN state IN ('Vic','Victoria') THEN 'VIC' WHEN state IN ('nsw','New South Wales') THEN 'NSW' WHEN state = 'Qld' THEN 'QLD' WHEN state = 'W.A.' THEN 'WA' WHEN state = 'Tas' THEN 'TAS' ELSE state END AS clean_state, COUNT(*) FROM customers GROUP BY clean_state;

module: 6. Clean data and tell the story
title: Duplicate customers
task: Find email addresses that belong to more than one customer once you ignore upper and lower case. Show the lower-case email and how many customers have it.
answer: SELECT LOWER(email) AS email, COUNT(*) FROM customers GROUP BY LOWER(email) HAVING COUNT(*) > 1;

module: 6. Clean data and tell the story
title: The May mystery
task: For April, May and June 2025, show each month, each marketing channel name and how many orders came from customers of that channel.
answer: SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', o.order_date) AS month, ch.channel_name, COUNT(*) FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN channels ch ON ch.channel_id = c.channel_id WHERE o.order_date BETWEEN '2025-04-01' AND '2025-06-30' GROUP BY month, ch.channel_name;
